Design & checks

The existing internal-gear arrangement now has a module-1 264T ring and solid 12T pinion, giving 22:1 instead of 6:1. The 296 mm ring replaces the previous 224 mm experimental ring. The motor centre moves out to 126 mm and the four tilted rollers follow the enlarged track. A 688ZZ bearing supports the pinion close to the teeth.

Two rear braces and two swept front braces support the tower from both sides. The front pair attaches to six existing 31 mm grid inserts on the fixed Z actuator lid, then slopes forward around the radial stage to the far deck edge. The Z support’s lower flange reaches the full 148 mm ring radius; its outer mounting bolts sit at a 138 mm radius. The fixed base and stand are now 312 mm square, and the rear deck extends 180 mm from the rotation axis. Its 296 × 328 mm footprint fits the H2S with 4 mm bed margin when rotated on the bed. The support keeps its flat outer print face and 31 mm actuator grid. This tab uses the 4× Z actuator and 1× radial actuator; the original assembly remains available.

At 250 mm reach, a 1.8° motor with 1/16 microstepping commands about 0.022 mm per increment (previously 0.082 mm). This is nominal resolution, not measured accuracy. Backlash, ring runout and vibration need a printed test. No soft isolators are added between the probe and its base.

The explosion separates service modules, with actuator internals and the ring/deck/support kept together. Rotation returns to zero while exploded. Press fits and released threads are documented exceptions to rigid interference checks.
